title: Embargoed rollout dashboard guardrails — lab notes
body:
Purpose
This is a lab-style set of notes for designing observability guardrails for embargoed (private-stage) rollouts. The goal is a compact, repeatable checklist teams can follow when they want to stage a model or routing change behind an embargo (limited audience/internal-only) while minimizing query cost and protecting PII in traces.

Audience
- Observability owners, oncall, SRE, applied-ML release engineers, product owners running closed canaries.

Background and problem statement
- Embargoed rollouts happen frequently for private beta customers, early canaries, and security reviews.
- Typical problems we see: dashboards are noisy, query costs spike, traces leak sensitive prompt/context from early customers, and oncall lacks a compact view to decide go/no-go.
- This doc stitches together a minimal metric/trace set, sampling guidance, and a query-budget estimation technique suitable for a private canary window (1–72 hours).

Objectives
1) Define a minimal metric contract that surfaces regressions (latency, error, quality drop) without flooding panels.
2) Provide deterministic trace-sampling rules for embargoed sessions that protect PII and keep samples actionable.
3) Offer a lightweight query-budget estimator for dashboard panels and scheduled probes.
4) Produce a short rollout checklist operators can run in <20 minutes before enabling embargoed traffic.

Minimal metric contract (per-route where possible)
- approx_time_to_first_token_ms: p50/p95/p99 (describe user-perceived latency)
- generate_error_rate: categorical errors / total requests (include model fallback and infra errors)
- kvcache_hit_rate: ratio of requests that used cache prefix (for workloads that rely on prefix caching)
- output_quality_signal: surrogate score derived from a small eval set or synthetic prompt (see below)
- drop_in_throughput_pct: relative throughput vs baseline pooled model (important for Dedicated allocations)
Notes on definitions:
- output_quality_signal should be computed from a deterministic mini-eval run (see section "synthetic prompt harness") and be comparably small (<=50 queries per minute) and tagged embargoed=true.
- metric names should be prefixed with embargo.stage (e.g., embargo.stage.latency.p95) so dashboards can filter quickly.

Tracing & PII guardrails
- Do not capture raw prompt or free-text responses in traces for embargoed sessions. Replace with hashed prompt fingerprint and high-level tag buckets (e.g., prompt_template=invoice_extract).
- Trace attributes to include: embargo_id, route, model_version, customer_tier (internal|beta|pilot), token_count, kv_prefetch (bool), inference_node_id.
- Sampling policy: deterministic hashing on embargo_id + session_id with a cap. For small embargoes use sampling_rate=1.0 but limit retained traces to N=200 per hour by performing a downstream write-throttle in the trace-collector. For larger canaries, use sampling_rate=0.05 with burst allowance (first 10 sessions fully sampled).
- Redaction pipeline: ensure trace exporter strips PHI/PII fields before writing to long-term retention. For embargoed traces we prefer short retention (7 days) unless explicitly escalated.

Dashboard layout recommendations (compact, operator-first)
- Top row (go/no-go quick glance): p95 latency, generate_error_rate, output_quality_signal (mini-eval), traffic_fraction (embargo vs baseline). Display numeric delta vs baseline with color rules.
- Middle row (investigation anchors): throughput, kvcache_hit_rate, tail latency heatmap (tokenized heatmap by stage), and model_version split.
- Bottom row (cost & tracing): query-budget consumption (see estimator below), number of retained traces, average tokens per request.
- Widget behavior: default to embargo-only filter; a single click toggles to baseline comparison. Provide a small dropdown to switch trace sampling view (sampled, last-N).

Mini-eval / synthetic prompt harness (for quality_signal)
- Keep this harness deterministic and cheap: 30 curated prompts representative of critical user journeys. Run at a cadence of 1/min or 5/min depending on risk.
- Evaluate a small set of metrics: exact_match_ratio (when applicable), semantic-similarity-batch (embedding cosine threshold), and a short hallucination-count proxy (keyword hallucination heuristics).
- Tag results embargo.stage and embargo.id. Track delta vs baseline model to catch regressions quickly.

Query-budget estimator (simple method operators can run)
Inputs (operator-supplied):
- estimated_panel_refresh_rate_minutes (R) — how often dashboards refresh queries; default 1 minute for real-time panels, 5–15 for investigative panels.
- number_of_panels (P) — panels in embargo dashboard (e.g., 8).
- avg_query_cost_per_panel (C) — historical average query cost in cost units (our internal meter) per execution. This can be approximated from past dashboards; default = 0.12 cost-units per panel query.
- probe_queries_per_minute (S) — synthetic probe queries (mini-eval) per minute.
Estimator formula (minute basis):
Total_minute_cost = (P / R) * C + S * C_probe
Where C_probe is cost per probe (approx equal to a single panel query or slightly higher; default 0.2).
Examples:
- 8 panels refreshing every 1 minute, C=0.12 => dashboard_cost_per_min = (8/1)*0.12 = 0.96 cost-units/min = ~58 cost-units/hour. Add probes S=1/min * 0.2 = 0.2 -> total 1.16/min.
- Guidance: keep embargo dashboards under 100 cost-units/hour for short windows. If exceeding, increase R for noncritical panels or replace expensive widgets with pre-aggregated metrics.

Alerting & canary gating rules
- Soft alert (notify slack + ticket): output_quality_signal delta > 7% sustained for 3 consecutive samples OR generate_error_rate > baseline by +1.5x for 5 minutes.
- Hard gate (auto-fallback): p95 latency > 3x baseline OR generate_error_rate > 10% absolute AND at least two corroborating signals (kvcache_drop or throughput_loss).
- Alerts should include embargo_id, sample links, and the last synthetic probe payload results. Avoid including raw prompts.

Operational checklist (pre-embargo flip, <20 minutes)
1) Ensure embargo dashboard exists and default filter = embargo_id+internal_only.
2) Confirm synthetic harness is enabled and returning stable baseline numbers (run 30 quick probes).
3) Validate trace-sampling rule for embargo_id (hashing deterministic and cap applied).
4) Run query-budget estimator with operator-specified R/P and confirm within acceptable bound or increase R.
5) Ensure retention policy for embargoed traces set to 7d and that export redaction flag is enabled.
6) Add a short-lived Slack channel with alert webhook and a named oncall (<=1 person).
7) Start with traffic_fraction <= 0.5% and increase slowly with pre-defined checkpoints (0.5, 2, 10, 50, 100%).

Post-embargo wrap-up (within 48h)
- Run a short audit: dashboard query-cost ledger, sample of retained traces validation (redaction), and synthetic-harness comparison across stages.
- Convert any useful embargo-only widgets into production-level panels if they prove valuable for long-term ops.

Implementation notes & quick references
- Implementation ticket template: Jira OBS-412 (use as starting checklist).
- Example trace-sampling code snippet (pseudocode):
  if hash(embargo_id + session_id) % 100 < sampling_pct*100 and traces_retained_hour < 200: retain_trace() else: discard_or_minimal()
- Short hand for DBA/metrics: when in doubt pre-aggregate in metrics pipeline (reduce query cost) rather than rely on expensive live SQL panels.

Open questions / follow-ups
- How strict should embargo trace retention be for pilot customers where legal requires longer retention? (action: security to define policy)
- Can we add a toggle to embargo dashboards to move expensive widgets into a cost-sandboxed mode? (action: obs-console team)
- Do we need an automatic embargo-snapshot export that packs last-1h into a zipped redacted artifact for audits? (action: infra)

Appendix: quick color rule suggestions
- green: metric within +/-2% of baseline
- yellow: delta 2–7% or p95 latency increase <1.5x
- red: delta >7% or p95 latency >1.5x or error_rate > 3% absolute

Notes and provenance
- Ran initial experiment in Q4 2025 with internal beta group (pilot-ember). Observability team curated 24 synthetic prompts and capped trace retention to 7 days. Results: reduced dashboard query cost by 64% relative to unfiltered panels and reduced sensitive-field exposure by adding prompt fingerprinting.

Short-term owners
- Observability: Aisha Patel (doc owner), Miguel Torres (dashboard lead), Rina Sato (tracing), Danielle O'Connor (synthetic harness).

End of notes
